prompt: Evidence linking the Mediterranean diet to cardiovascular health outcomes
report:
# Mediterranean Diet and Cardiovascular Health

## Trial evidence
The PREDIMED randomized trial found that a Mediterranean diet supplemented with extra-virgin olive oil or nuts reduced major cardiovascular events versus a low-fat control [S1][S2]. The effect was driven mainly by fewer strokes [S2].

## Cohort evidence
Large prospective cohort studies associate higher adherence to the Mediterranean pattern with lower cardiovascular mortality [S3][S4]. A dose-response is observed across cohort quartiles of adherence [S4].

## Mechanisms
Proposed mechanisms include improved lipid profiles from olive oil monounsaturated fat, lower inflammation, and better endothelial function [S5].

## Bottom line
Converging trial and cohort evidence supports the Mediterranean diet, rich in olive oil, for cardiovascular risk reduction [S1][S3].

## Sources
[S1] https://www.nejm.org/predimed
[S2] https://www.bmj.com/predimed-stroke
[S3] https://www.thelancet.com/mediterranean-cohort
[S4] https://www.ahajournals.org/med-diet-mortality
[S5] https://www.health.harvard.edu/mediterranean-diet
